# Conclusions

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Key takeaways

**Least Squares:**

-   Fast and intuitive
-   Good for exploration
-   Limited uncertainty quantification
-   Sensitive to assumptions

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Maximum Likelihood:**

-   Principled statistical framework
-   Natural uncertainty quantification
-   Enables model comparison
-   More computationally intensive

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Bayesian inference and MCMC:**

-   Priors make assumptions explicit, and checkable
-   The posterior is the full answer: estimates, credible intervals, predictions
-   Metropolis is a few lines of code; the work is in tuning and diagnostics
-   Never trust a chain you have not checked

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Advanced Methods:**

-   Handle complex scenarios
-   Provide robust uncertainty
-   Require more expertise
-   Often computationally expensive

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Choosing the right method

**For Quick Exploration:** Least Squares

**For Publication:** Maximum Likelihood

**For Complex Models:** Bayesian Methods

**For Real-time:** Particle Filtering

**For Model Comparison:** ABC or MCMC

[**General Principle:**]{style="color: tomato;"} Start simple, add complexity as needed

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Final thoughts

[**Model fitting is both art and science:**]{style="color: tomato;"}

-   Requires domain expertise
-   Demands statistical rigor
-   Benefits from computational tools
-   Needs careful validation

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**The goal is not just to fit models, but to:**

-   Understand disease dynamics
-   Make reliable predictions
-   Inform policy decisions
-   Advance scientific knowledge

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Resources

### Full courses (free)

-   Model fitting and inference for infectious disease dynamics by Sebastian Funk, Anton Camacho, Helen Johnson, Amanda Minter, Kathleen O'Reilly and Nicholas Davies. [Link](https://sbfnk.github.io/mfiidd/index.html)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Core concepts

-   [Introduction to the Concept of Likelihood and Its Applications](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/2515245917744314)
-   *Key considerations for model fitting and calibration*: [Choices and trade-offs in inference with infectious disease models](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1755436519300441?via%3Dihub)
-   *A compilation of model fitting tutorials*: [Tooling-up for infectious disease transmission modelling](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1755436520300220)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Least squares

-   *Key tutorial on the least squares method*: [Fitting dynamic models to epidemic outbreaks with quantified uncertainty: A primer for parameter uncertainty, identifiability, and forecasts](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2468042717300234)
-   [Fitting Epidemic Models to Data by James Holland Jones](https://web.stanford.edu/class/earthsys214/notes/fit.html)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### MLE

-   [Fitting Epidemic Models to Data by James Holland Jones](https://web.stanford.edu/class/earthsys214/notes/fit.html)
-   *R tutorial on MLE*: [Estimating model parameters by maximum likelihood](https://daphnia.ecology.uga.edu/drakelab/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/likelihood.pdf)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Bayesian inference and MCMC

-   [Bayesian data analysis for newcomers](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13423-017-1272-1) (Kruschke & Liddell, 2018)
-   [A simple introduction to Markov Chain Monte–Carlo sampling](https://doi.org/10.3758/s13423-016-1015-8) (van Ravenzwaaij et al., 2018)
-   [Understanding the Metropolis–Hastings algorithm](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.1995.10476177) (Chib & Greenberg, 1995)
-   [Markov Chain Monte Carlo: an introduction for epidemiologists](https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyt043)
-   [Weak convergence and optimal scaling of random walk Metropolis algorithms](https://doi.org/10.1214/aoap/1034625254) (Roberts, Gelman & Gilks, 1997): the 23% rule

------------------------------------------------------------------------
